# How Kailash is built {#build-model}

Kailash is built declaratively from two Nix repositories: the **OS
repository** (the distribution flake) and the **packages repository**
(bespoke derivations and the tool overlay). The tool manifest is the
single source of truth — packaging, menus, CLI and generated docs all
derive from it; nothing is hand-maintained per surface.

## Pins and locks

No package floats:

- Bespoke tools are pinned upstream with `nvfetcher` and committed
  with content hashes; a pin changes only together with the manifest
  entry it belongs to.
- The `nixpkgs` lock stays put between scheduled refreshes; tools
  pinned inside the lock do not move.
- **The lockfile is the version.** A system moves forward when its
  operator pulls a newer lock, or when a release is adopted — never in
  the background.

## Generated surfaces

Everything the distribution publishes about its tools derives from the
manifest at build time. This guide follows the same rule: its per-tool
reference pages (Part III) are regenerated from the manifest and the
packaged tools' own interfaces, never hand-copied.
